subject: Pricing accommodation request — temporary rate accommodation for delayed feature-flag rollout

messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@nebula-labs.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: anna.lopez@nebula-labs.com
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Feature-flag delay and request for a temporary pricing accommodation

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Quick note from our side — the feature flag that Nebula planned to use to swap the Redwood inference pipeline into production is delayed on our end. Our infra vendor discovered an incompatibility with the nightly runtime (security hardening triggered a regression) and the engineering team pushed the go-live by ~6 weeks to give them time to validate the fix.

This timing hits our Q2 launch and creates a measurable business impact: marketing campaign and customer onboarding are both tied to the original go-live. Given the delay is on our side but directly caused by a Redwood runtime change we pulled in, we wanted to ask whether Redwood can consider a temporary pricing accommodation for the affected committed usage period while we complete validation.

Specifically, we'd like to discuss a billing adjustment for the first month after the original go-live date (effectively a one-off invoicing concession while the feature flag is unavailable). We expect to proceed with the integration once our validation completes in approximately 6 weeks.

Appreciate any flexibility — happy to hop on a 30-minute call today to go over numbers.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Engineering, Nebula Labs

Jonas / Karthik — forwarding Nebula's note. They are a strategic mid-market account (NEB-4983) and the go-live delay will push launch into a different quarter, which affects our attainment and their onboarding schedule.

Proposed internal ask: approve a temporary rate accommodation for one billing cycle tied to the original committed spend. I recommend we offer a pro-rated billing adjustment equivalent to 40% of their committed usage for the impacted month (not a recurring discount) plus extended onboarding support. This keeps the concession bounded and aligns incentives for Nebula to finish validation quickly.

Why this number: finance indicated that anything over 50% needs CFO approval; 40% can be approved by finance lead (Laura). We should also request a short mutual action plan (MAP) from the customer that lists milestones and the new go-live date to avoid open-ended concessions.

Attachments: deployment-timeline.xlsx (they included in their SOW).

Can you confirm approval to proceed with the 40% one-off adjustment and I will draft the billing note + MAP template to send to Nebula. If we need exec sign-off I can loop in Aditya.

- Marissa
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — I support the bounded approach but want product to confirm risk/ETA and Finance to sign off on the accounting treatment. I have two asks before we commit to the accommodation:

1) Product confirmation: Karthik, can you confirm the root cause (you mentioned runtime hardening) and whether the fix is isolated (i.e., will the same regression affect other customers)? Also confirm the expected timeline (any chance it slips beyond 6 weeks?) and whether we can offer a technical mitigation that reduces their exposure sooner.

2) Finance/legal: Laura, is the proposed 40% one-off accounting-acceptable as a "billing adjustment" (not a contract amendment) and can billing process it without requiring a revised SOW? If Finance requires a paper trail, Marissa should prepare a short amendment that references the MAP.

Marissa — hold on sending a formal offer until we have Karthik + Laura confirmations. If either asks for a higher/lower adjustment we can iterate, but I agree it should be non-recurring and tied to the MAP.

Jonas

Subject: Re: Feature-flag delay and request for a temporary pricing accommodation

Quick update from Product/Platform after reviewing the incident and cross-checking our runtime rollout notes.

Root cause: a compatibility regression introduced by the 2028.03.10 security hardening that surfaced in Nebula's downstream validation. The regression is isolated to a specific configuration path most customers don't use; we've flagged the fix as high priority and scheduled a targeted patch.

ETA: engineering estimates 5–6 weeks for validated patch and a safe feature-flag re-enable for Nebula's stack. There is a short mitigation we can offer (a configuration rollback for that path) that would reduce their exposure within 10 business days, but it requires a brief maintenance window and coordination with Nebula's infra team. If Nebula accepts the rollback, we expect the effective delay to be ~10 days instead of 6 weeks.

Recommendation to Sales/Finance: offer a narrow, non-recurring billing adjustment tied to the MAP. Given the mitigation option, I'd support a smaller one-off accommodation if Nebula is willing to take the rollback (e.g., 15% for the impacted month) — otherwise approve the 40% one-off adjustment if they prefer to avoid maintenance now. Please capture the customer's choice in the MAP and make the billing action contingent on it.

I'll prepare a short technical note for the MAP describing the rollback steps and expected risk window.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
